sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law - Quebec private law; Common Law - federal public, tax and regulatory law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application since 2017-09-21)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, in force for Canada 2018-12-30)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014-10-01)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC implementing regulations (SOR/2002-184 and subsequent amendments); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 83.05 (terrorist entity listing); United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 41; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17 (autonomous sanctions). Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (LPLE), arts 21.0.1-21.0.8 (significant control register) and Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 2 (registration and name rules).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Attestation de statut of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Competent Authority of the origin state (Canada accepted the Hague Apostille Convention effective 2024-01-11); consular legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate if the origin state is not an Apostille party; certified French translation by an OTTIAQ-certified translator for REQ filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or the licensing authority of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization as above, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Quebec attorney or representative (LPLE s. 27)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the signatory's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization of the foreign-executed POA; notarization in Quebec if the POA is executed in Quebec; certified French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or national identity documents of all individuals holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular officer in the document holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization for notarized copies made outside Canada; certified French translation attached where the notary certificate is not in French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent and identification of the mandatory representative domiciled in Quebec (if any general partner is not resident in Quebec)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The appointed resident representative, executed before a Quebec notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notarization only (no apostille required); underlying foreign POA remains subject to apostille/legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, directors and officers of corporate general partners, and authorized signatories against (i) the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, (ii) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Criminal Code s. 83.05 terrorist entity list, and (iii) the OFAC SDN List as a prudential overlay for USD-denominated Apple App Store and Google Play payouts. Screening results must be documented in the LP's CDD file and re-run upon any change in significant control and at least every 180 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Centre d'inscription en ligne: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, the raison sociale of a Quebec societe en commandite must be in French or qualify as deemed French. The name must include the mention 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 's.e.c.' (or 'LP' only as a supplementary descriptor), and must contain the name of at least one general partner. Non-French distinctive elements are permitted only as proper names or where a French generic term is present; transliteration must follow OQLF graphic rules. REQ may refer the file to the Office quebecois de la langue francaise (OQLF) for a conformity certificate when the proposed name contains non-French components.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (OSFI chartered bank authorization required)
Compagnie de fiducie / Trust company (authorization required)
Courtier / Broker (securities or investment dealer licensing required)
Universite, College, Ecole (Education Ministry consent required)
Avocat, Notaire, Comptable professionnel agre, Ingenieur, Medecin (reserved professional titles)
Parti politique / Political party (electoral authority consent required)
Canada / Quebec (wording implying Crown patronage or public authority status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not extendable; upon expiry a new reservation request and statutory fee are required. If REQ refuses the proposed name: (1) file a written demand for re-examination (demande de revision) with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal, attaching a legal opinion on conformity with the Charter of the French Language and the reservation receipt; (2) if the objection is linguistic, obtain an OQLF certificate of conformity / visa and re-submit; (3) if REQ maintains the refusal, reserve a new name with a modified distinctive element under the same French generic term; (4) as a final remedy, apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, arts. 529 et seq., noting that litigation will delay formation and should be reserved for material rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. REQ prohibits PO Boxes as the sole address and requires a real civic address in Quebec serving as the LP's siege social / service address under a valid lease or service agreement. A full-service virtual office provider offering a physical street address, mail receipt, service of process acceptance, and document access satisfies LPLE requirements for a low-risk software publisher. A mailbox-only virtual service, or one where the address is shared by multiple unrelated registrants, creates substantive compliance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Base-case probability: 10% in the first 12 months for a low-risk software publishing LP at a compliant virtual office. Probability rises to 25% or higher where the registered address is mailbox-only or shared among more than five unrelated registrants, as REQ conducts targeted unannounced address-integrity campaigns and acts on third-party complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ, c. P-44.1), arts. 3-10, 18-24, 34-35; Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236-2250 (limited partnership); Charter of the French Language (RLRQ, c. C-11).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the amount and form of contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement. No escrow account or government deposit is required for a Quebec limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The undersigned general partner accepts the formation of the Quebec limited partnership under the name set out in the declaration of registration; (2) the registered office shall be established at the address specified in Schedule A, and the partnership may so designate in the declaration; (3) the contributions of limited and general partners are hereby subscribed in accordance with the executed limited partnership agreement, no statutory minimum capital being required; (4) [Name] is appointed as the person charged with managing the partnership’s daily operations and as representative before the Registraire des entreprises and Revenu Québec; (5) the officers are authorized to pay all filing fees and to open bank accounts after issuance of the certificate of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a compulsory search of the Registraire’s enterprise name database to confirm availability. Submit an online name reservation request for the proposed limited partnership name, ensuring compliance with French-language requirements of the Charter of the French Language. The name must include a legal element identifying it as a limited partnership or 'société en commandite'.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name
Statutory declaration of French-language name compliance
Identification documents of the general partner
Description of principal business activity (ISIC 5820)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended name reservation with corrected distinctive and descriptive elements, or submit a written administrative review request to the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a limited partnership agreement in accordance with Civil Code of Québec articles 2236-2250, setting out capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, management powers of the general partner, and restrictions on limited partners. Concurrently prepare the Déclaration d'immatriculation in the form required by the Registraire. Notarization is required only if an immovable is contributed to the partnership.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Schedule of partner contributions
Registered office address in Quebec
Full civil identification of general partner(s)
ISIC/NAICS activity code declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any drafting ambiguities prior to filing. If notarial redrafting is required for an immovable contribution, obtain a corrigendum to the partnership agreement before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing service (eRegistre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Quebec Enterprise Registrar’s online portal, select 'Immatriculer une société en commandite', enter the name reservation number, complete the statutory declaration, upload supporting documents, pay the required filing fee, and submit. Upon acceptance, the Registraire issues the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
Name reservation certificate
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
Identification documents of the general partner
Power of attorney if filing through an authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried for incompleteness, use the Registraire's online correction service to cure minor omissions. For substantive refusal, file an administrative review application or seek judicial review before the Court of Québec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for GST/HST and QST with Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec / Agence du revenu du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued by the Registraire, apply online to Revenu Québec to open a GST/HST account and a Québec Sales Tax (QST) account. Indicate that the entity is a limited partnership with pass-through taxation. If the partnership will have employees in Quebec, simultaneously register for employer source deductions and CNESST occupational health account.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate issued by the Registraire
Certified copy of the declaration of registration
Limited partnership agreement
Tax identification / SIN of individual partners or legal entity ID of corporate partners
Registered office address and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If accounts are not opened within the service standard, contact Revenu Québec business services via the 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' portal, or submit a compliant application form LM-1/VF manually.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Corporate Records, and Governance Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formalize the registered office address in Quebec, create the partnership minute book and statutory registers, retain the executed partnership agreement and declaration of registration, issue partnership interest statements, and execute the banking authorization resolution enabling the partnership to receive Apple App Store and Google Play payouts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Registraire
Executed general partner resolutions
Bank account opening package
AML/KYC due diligence records for beneficial owners
Registered office confirmation letter from landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor raises KYC objections, provide a certified extract from the Registraire des entreprises and a legal opinion confirming the general partner's authority to bind the partnership.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing board mandates a permit for ISIC 5820 software publishing; municipal business licensing may apply only for a physical office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating license required; a municipal occupancy or business permit may be required if the partnership maintains a physical establishment in Quebec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – intangible software publishing; no EIA, attestation, or authorization required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or waste discharge from server-driven MMORPG publishing; any retired electronic equipment must be managed under Quebec's residual materials and e-waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational health and safety clearance required from CNESST for any Quebec office; municipal fire safety inspection and building occupancy permit required under the Quebec Fire Safety Code and Construction Code. If a server room or data center is housed, a structural load certification must be submitted to the municipal building authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial tax administration; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for LP legal registration. Primary portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-account.html); Revenu Québec clic Revenu Québec (https://clic.revenuquebec.ca); Registraire d'entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec société en commandite (LP): (1) file a declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ (Québec enterprise number); (2) apply to CRA via Business Registration Online or Form RC1 for a Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST 'RT' program account; (3) register with Revenu Québec for QST using Form LM-101-V or the online clic Revenu Québec portal once taxable supplies in Quebec exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; (4) file annual T5013 (federal) and CO-17 (Quebec) partnership information returns and report income allocations to partners; (5) for non-resident partners, evaluate Canadian Part I filing obligations under ITA s.115 for Canadian-source partnership income and apply Part XIII withholding to any interest, rent, or royalty components distributed, reporting via Form NR4 and obtaining non-resident partner declarations to establish whether the partnership constitutes a 'foreign partnership' for CRA purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime; a Limited Partnership is statutorily fiscally transparent. Available elections and designations: (a) ITA s.103 partnership income/loss allocation election where the allocation is reasonable; (b) ITA s.220(3.1) off-calendar fiscal-period election, with Form T1139 filing; (c) Excise Tax Act s.156 election for GST/HST treatment of transactions between closely related registrants (limited utility for an LP); (d) compliance positions and designations under Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (BEPS Action 2) applicable to partnership interests causing deduction/non-inclusion mismatches; (e) QST reporting-frequency election with Revenu Québec (monthly/quarterly/annual); and (f) for non-resident partners, an NR6 undertaking to reduce Part XIII withholding where appropriate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST); both are transaction-based value-added taxes with zero-rating for exports. On Quebec taxable supplies, the combined headline consumer rate is 5.000% federal GST + 9.975% Quebec QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: the GST/HST small-supplier threshold (Excise Tax Act s.148(1)) is exceeded when total worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; the parallel QST threshold is aligned at CAD 30,000 under the Act respecting the Québec Sales Tax. For non-resident digital suppliers of intangible personal property to Quebec consumers, registration with CRA and Revenu Québec is required once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded, while a person carrying on business in Canada may also be required to register regardless of threshold. Voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction controls, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. E-invoicing is optional; the Pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard is endorsed. Registrants must file and remit electronically through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE and Revenu Québec's clic Revenu Québec portal. Non-resident digital merchants must use CRA's simplified non-resident GST/HST registration and remittance portal. No API-based invoice authentication, clearance, or cryptographic stamping is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Quebec LP supplying MMORPG downloadable games, in-app virtual property, and platform support services to Apple/Google (non-resident platform operators) or directly to end users located outside Canada qualifies for zero-rating under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V, item 17 (services supplied to non-residents) and item 22 (intangible personal property supplied for use outside Canada), with equivalent QST zero-rating mirroring the federal list. Under the July 1, 2021 federal digital platform supply rules, where App Store/Google Play control the essential elements of the supply, the platform is deemed to make the taxable supply to the Canadian consumer, and the LP's underlying B2B supply to the non-resident platform is not subject to GST/HST/QST. The CRA's digital services place-of-supply rules generally deem a supply to occur at the recipient's normal residence, supporting zero-rating for non-Canadian geolocated end users. To claim the 0% rate and substantiate any net GST/HST/QST refund, the LP must retain contemporaneous evidence of non-residency, including platform attestations, billing addresses, IP geolocation logs, and ordinary invoice or transaction records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement evidencing principal-to-principal supplies to non-resident platform operators
Platform payout statements, payment processor settlement records, and inward remittance advices evidencing receipt of consideration from outside Canada
Contemporaneous non-residency evidence: billing addresses, IP geolocation logs, platform attestations, and end-user country records
If physical media is exported (e.g., collector's discs): Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A), bill of lading or air waybill, commercial invoice, and proof of outward movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal 4-year limitation period, extended to 8 years for misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud. Penalties include: Excise Tax Act s.280 (false statements or omissions) CAD 100 to CAD 10,000; s.285 (wilful evasion) 50% of the net tax evaded; s.285.1 (false deduction or refund claim) CAD 1,000; s.239 criminal offences with fines and imprisonment; and s.323 director liability for unremitted GST/HST. Quebec's Tax Administration Act provides a 50% penalty under s.59 where a person is reckless, fines up to CAD 100,000 for s.58/59 contraventions, and statutory interest under s.28. Insufficient export documentation triggers denial of the 0% rate, clawback of input tax credits and refunds, recalculation as taxable Canadian supplies, and interest charges. While Canada has no codified 180-day FX repatriation deadline, prolonged failure to repatriate export proceeds is an audit red flag and may be treated as evidence that the supply was not genuinely made to a non-resident, leading to reassessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is decentralized and conducted through federally regulated deposit-taking institutions under the supervision of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Quebec financial-market conduct for payment services is overseen by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency under a floating exchange-rate regime with no current-account exchange controls. The Canadian dollar is freely transferable for both capital and current transactions; non-resident investors may repatriate capital and profits without quantitative limits. Profit remittances from a Quebec limited partnership distribution to non-resident limited partners are, however, subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and to Quebec tax rules where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts, including proceeds from global MMORPG in-app sales routed through Apple App Store and Google Play, may be retained in foreign currency, provided the underlying economic reality is reflected in Canadian-dollar functional-currency financial statements and any foreign-exchange gain or loss is recognized for tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not authorized deposit-taking institutions in Canada and cannot provide a domestic clearing or CDIC-insured cash account. They can be used as supplemental payout-aggregation rails for Apple App Store and Google Play receipts, but the provider must comply with Canadian anti-money-laundering obligations as a foreign money services business under FINTRAC if it delivers payment services in Canada. The primary treasury account must remain with a Schedule I bank to ensure regulatory certainty and access to Payments Canada clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch interview is not universally mandatory because Canadian Schedule I banks permit remote video onboarding under FINTRAC requirements when the applicant provides full due-diligence documentation. However, for a newly formed Quebec limited partnership with non-resident limited partners or complex beneficial ownership, banks commonly require at least one key principal or the corporate general partner's authorized signatory to attend a physical or video interview with the bank's compliance officer. The general partner must execute the account charter, and all signatories must have verified identity and proof of authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through limited partnership structure with opaque limited partner ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The full limited partnership agreement, a notarized certificate of incumbency, a current extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, a complete beneficial-ownership chart, tax identification numbers for all partners, and source-of-wealth statements for each limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume in-app purchase receipts routed through Apple and Google foreign payout entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple/Google payout statements showing gross and net proceeds, a reconciliation ledger mapping payout streams to the bank account, FINTRAC money-services-business registration if payment services are performed, a documented AML compliance program, transaction-monitoring procedures, and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and cross-border corporate ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports or government-issued ID, proof of residential address, bank or professional references, original board resolutions approving account opening, signed delegated authority documents, and a legal opinion from Quebec counsel confirming the validity of the limited partnership and the foreign entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-time capital injection from an overseas related company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice, executed subscription agreements, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, full organizational chart of the funding affiliate, wire instruction with a transparent capital-contribution purpose code, and confirmation from the sending bank that the payment is not structured to avoid reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from foreign limited partners should be routed through the SWIFT MT103 wire network with a clearly stated purpose code matching the receiving bank's capital-subscription classification. The sending bank must transmit full originator and beneficiary information in compliance with the travel rule and FINTRAC electronic-fund-transfer reporting thresholds. The receiving bank requires the executed subscription agreement, the capital call notice, an updated register of partners, and confirmation that the contribution is an equity injection rather than a loan. If the investment crosses applicable thresholds, the bank may request evidence that the transaction complies with the Investment Canada Act and Quebec enterprise-registration requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for MMORPG development, cloud infrastructure, and third-party publishing services should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for open-account vendor payments and through an irrevocable commercial letter of credit for documentary trade transactions requiring shipment control. CAD payments clear through Payments Canada via Lynx for large-value real-time settlement and ACSS for batch retail clearing. USD payments clear through the bank's correspondent network in the United States. Apple and Google payouts arrive by wire or ACH to the designated treasury account and must be reconciled to app-store sales reports before operational disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian Schedule I bank or registered authorized dealer for hedging expected net USD revenue from app-store payouts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with an authorized bank dealer when settlement is required in CAD and the foreign-currency notional is used only to hedge genuine economic exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term foreign-currency liability transformation
OTC currency options under an ISDA/CSA collateral arrangement, limited to hedging transactional exposure and not speculative trading

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) general corporate rate; the Quebec Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under ITA s.96 and the Quebec Taxation Act, so entity-level income is not taxed and the combined rate applies to corporate partners only.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No small business deduction at the LP level; relevant credits available upon allocation: federal SR&ED investment tax credit (35% refundable for qualifying CCPC or individual partners; 15% non-refundable for large corporations), Quebec refundable multimedia tax credit up to 30% of eligible labor and computer expenditures for certified interactive digital media/MMORPG production, accelerated CCA on servers and capitalized game development software, and immediate expensing of eligible Canadian software and manufacturing/processing equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 / T5013-SUM — Partnership Information Return; filed electronically with the CRA via E-file using certified software, or through CRA Represent a Client / My Business Account; paper filing permitted only in limited cases.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the last day of the fifth month following the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end); T5013 slips must be furnished to all partners no later than the same statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, BN/UPI, head office address in Quebec, fiscal period, ISIC 5820/NAICS 511210 business code, and platform identifiers for Apple App Store and Google Play payout streams.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate whether any limited partner is a non-resident and list each partner's country of residence; identify the non-resident general partner, if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from in-app purchases, subscriptions, and licensing; deductions for app store commissions, hosting, salaries, amortization of capitalized development costs, and arm's-length intercompany fees; net active business income or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Canadian-source active business income to non-resident partners; apply the same deductible allocation rules and functional-currency reporting as for resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Proportional allocation of net income or loss to each general and limited partner under the LP agreement, including carried-interest waterfalls; issue T5013 slips reflecting each partner's share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, report TIN, treaty country, and enforce the mandatory 15% remittance under ITA s.153 for Canadian-source business income allocated or credited to the non-resident partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013: ITA s.162(7) penalty equal to the greater of C$100 and C$25 per partner per month late, capped at 24 months; per-slip penalties of C$25 to C$100 per T5013 slip (maximum C$2,500); parallel penalties apply under the Quebec Tax Administration Act and Revenu Québec may disallow deductions otherwise allowable to the LP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Relevé 16 (RL-16) — Amounts Allocated from a Partnership; filed with Revenu Québec through the Clic / Mon Entreprise portal, including the annual RL-16 summary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: RL-16 slips and summary must be filed with Revenu Québec no later than the last day of February following the calendar year in which the allocation occurred; partners must receive their RL-16 slips by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: LP name, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), federal business number, fiscal year-end, and address of the Quebec establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark non-resident partners and record jurisdiction of residence; the Quebec establishment income must be segregated from foreign-source amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — Share of Business Income (Loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's allocable share of Quebec-source MMORPG operating income computed under the Quebec Taxation Act, consistent with the T5013 allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the Quebec establishment; exclude intercompany dividends and capital gains not allocated to Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C — Management Fees, Interest, and Royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made by the LP to any partner for services, financing, or intellectual property, whether or not the recipient is a partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose fees or royalties paid to a non-resident partner separately; these may be subject to Part XIII / Quebec withholding unless a treaty exemption applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec late filing and omission penalties: C$25–C$100 per missing or late RL-16 slip, escalating daily penalties for repeated non-compliance, administrative fines up to C$5,000, and ministerial penalties for false statements; persistent default may also trigger a full audit of the LP and its partners.
